newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Whitbread doubles expansion plans.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Whitbread doubles expansion plans.

text.p: Brewer to leisure group Whitbread Plc plans to open another 250 high street restaurants and pubs this year at a cost of some 400 million pounds, creating about 5,000 jobs, chief executive designate David Thomas said on Wednesday.

In an interview Thomas said the company will develop about 80 Whitbread Inns, turning them into Hogshead or Brewers Fayre pubs, and open 40 Travel Inns, 45 more Pizza Huts, 35 Costa Coffee's and 40 Pelican restaurants -- mainly French style bistros Cafe Rouge and Cafe Dome.
Last year it opened 140 new outlets at a cost of some 300 million pounds.

Thomas told Reuters of the group's expansion plans shortly after the company announced its full year results to March 1, 1997 showing a 12 percent increase in pretax, pre-exceptional profits to 316.5 million pounds.
He also made positive remarks about current trading conditions, saying the company is "quite pleased" with the first two months of trading although the consumer is still very value conscious.
"We are quite pleased with the first two months. We have seen a strong build up of consumer confidence over the last year, but the consumer is still very well aware of value," Thomas said.
Whitbread is "reasonably confident" that the introduction of a national minimum wage, a manifesto pledge of the newly-elected Labour party, would not affect its business, Thomas said.
The company employs some 80,000 people and a large number of unskilled young bar staff.
"It is very much dependent on how it (minimum wage) is set," he said, "We are pretty confident of a good dialogue with politicians going forward."
The company would like to see incentive schemes and training costs taken into account as well as regional variations in standards of living.
"The consumer is not really unnerved at this stage and everything we have heard so far from the Labour party implies consumer confidence will remain high."
He pointed to Whitbread's advance hotel bookings, up two to three percent on the same time last year.

Whitbread shares ended the day at 798 pence, up eight pence on the day as were helped by a positive outlook from the company. The group's profits came out in the middle of brokers forecasts ranging from 313 to 321 million pounds.
Thomas said the company plans to sell off underperforming assets in the coming year, to raise some 100 million pounds as a minimum target.
The disposal programme will include the sale of Keg North America, Richardson Inns, and the group's remaining three star unbranded hotels as well its poor performing off-licenses and pubs.

The buoyant state of the property market means the company can expect better prices while removing its poor performing pubs and restaurants will improve the group's overall return on capital, he said.
This will ensure that its retail estate remains fresh and allows it to re-invest more heavily in contemporary sites and strongly branded areas, he said.
"Retailing is about, location, location, location," said Thomas, who takes over as chief executive from Peter Jarvis in June.
Whitbread is currently in a consolidation phase after a radical transformation from a pure brewing company to a mainly leisure and hotels business in less than five years.

It has spent heavily in the last two years, acquiring the 16-strong Marriott hotel chain in Britain, David Lloyd Leisure sports clubs and the Cafe Dome and Cafe Rouge which form part of the Pelican restaurant chain.
Turnover grew 10 percent to just over 3.0 billion pounds with like for like sales growing around four percent, said Whitbread.
The managed pub estate, which includes 337 Brewers Fayre pub-restaurants, grew profits 14 percent to 146.8 million pounds with total food sales up 19 percent.
In the restaurant and leisure division, which includes Beefeater Inns, T.G.I. Friday's, Pizza Hut, Costa Coffee trading profits were up 38 percent at 121.9 million pounds.

The beer company reported profits by 11 percent to 49.9 million with the best brand performance coming from lager Stella Artois which grew sales 20 percent to over one million barrels. Whitbread share of the British beer market rose to its highest all time level of 15.3 percent.
Profits from its pub estate fell 2.7 percent to 57.6 million after a reduction in the estate of 292 pubs -- Whitbread now owns 2,137 tied pubs and 195 leased free of the tie.

The group's four star Marriott hotels grew profits 22 percent with occupancy levels up 4.5 percentage points at 75.5 percent. Sports clubs David Lloyd Leisure improved its trading profit by 46 percent.
